active_question.title: Validate one provider-enabled bounded executor task
active_question.summary: One controlled attempt established that the deployment-local provider launcher did not start in the minimal executor image; provider connectivity was not exercised and no policy expansion occurred.

current_hypothesis.statement: One fixed Gemini patch-and-test executor profile can complete through the existing exact-host CONNECT attachment while keeping direct egress blocked and credentials outside worktree, output, and audit surfaces.
success_criteria: The fixed provider task reaches SUCCEEDED with a usable provider response and one disposable synthetic-file change.
The task retains the four bounded review artifacts, keeps source and direct egress isolated, and replays without re-execution.
failure_criteria: Gemini returns availability, authentication, quota, invalid-model, or new-endpoint failure; the single attempt then stops.
The task requests an unapproved hostname or requires policy expansion.
primary_metrics: artifact retention, source preservation, and idempotent replay
baseline_refs: prior Gemini deny-first probe: exact CONNECT destination only

active_experiment.purpose: Run exactly one fixed provider-enabled patch-and-test task through the existing RelayMe API.
active_experiment.design: Register one local-only Gemini profile with the fixed rootless sandbox, opaque credential profile, and exact prevalidated CONNECT attachment; execute once, inspect via RelayMe, replay once, then remove the profile attachment and runtime secret material.
active_experiment.backend: existing RelayMe test host rootless Podman
active_experiment.result_summary: The one retained task failed in 962 ms before any provider CONNECT because the host-built dynamically linked Go launcher could not start in the minimal executor image. Replay returned the original reviewable failed result; cleanup removed the entire temporary provider overlay.

findings.summary: With keep-id, Agent-owned mounts are visible as the Agent numeric identity while the image process remains a different primary identity. Protected output writes fail; the current group-writable disposable worktree and existing test file remain writable through a supplementary Agent group.
evidence: Both namespace-map forms were captured from inside the container and from a live keep-id container.
Fresh ordinary and disposable-worktree probes used network none, a read-only root filesystem, no provider material, and confirmed the existing fixed test file behavior.
All temporary containers, worktrees, and outputs were removed.

findings.summary: The fixed Agent-local identity mode paired with keep-id produced the Agent identity inside the rootless container and made both protected mounts writable without adding privilege, network, or client authority.
evidence: Local regression rejects unsupported, unpaired, client-supplied, and brief-supplied identity controls.
The isolated real-host fixed task retained all bounded review artifacts, preserved the source repository, cleaned its worktree/container, and replayed the retained result.
No provider credential, provider egress, or production resource was used.

findings.summary: The first provider-enabled executor acceptance stopped before network use: the fixed Go launcher was dynamically linked for the host and the minimal executor image lacked its dynamic loader. This is a deployment launcher/image compatibility defect, not a RelayMe Core or egress-policy defect.
evidence: The single RelayMe task retained exit code 255 and the bounded error that the fixed launcher could not be executed.
The exact idempotency replay returned the same execution ID and retained reviewable result with no changed files.
The proxy audit recorded only attachment preparation and release for the task, with no CONNECT event; direct network remained unavailable to the sandbox.
The temporary profile, credential copy, scoped client, proxy policy, launcher/image, source fixture, and worktree were removed after the attempt.

candidate_next_experiments.summary: After separately authorizing a new one-shot attempt, build the fixed provider launcher statically or against the executor image runtime, then repeat the same exact-host test without changing RelayMe Core or broadening the egress policy.
